newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen firmer in line with strong yen bonds.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen firmer in line with strong yen bonds.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended the day session firmer on Monday in line with the bullish yen bond market and in response to weak Tokyo share prices, traders said.

Bond market sentiment became bullish after a Bank of Japan (BOJ) quarterly report on Friday predicted a slowdown in economic growth in the first half of next fiscal year due to the effects of fiscal tightening.
The bull run of the fixed income sector across the yield curve is also due to weak Tokyo shares, which were again hurt by renewed concerns over the nation's banking sector.
"The BOJ report, along with dwindling shares, loosened the purse strings of even the most cautious investors and made them park money in the debt market," said a city bank trader.
Without those incentives, investors would have stayed out of the market, which has been floating at historically high levels.
The next benchmark, the December, also ended on a strong note at 99.23, compared with Friday's 99.19.

A shift in the benchmark status from the September to the December will officially take place when the December's combined turnover during the day and night sessions exceeds that of the September on two consecutive business days.
The shift may take place on Tuesday, traders said.
The BOJ injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market on Monday, maintaining its neutral stance.
The key overnight call rate was most heavily traded at 0.49 percent compared with Friday's weighted average of 0.47 percent.
